narration: A major political dispute can compete with economic policy for the attention of government officials. Legislative discussions, public debates, and institutional resources may become heavily focused on the impeachment proceedings. This could affect the pace of other government priorities, including budget deliberations, infrastructure development, and economic reforms. However, political attention being diverted does not automatically mean that government programs will stop. Government agencies continue to have responsibilities, and many projects operate under established budgets and administrative processes. The real concern arises when political conflict creates actual delays, weakens coordination, or prevents important decisions from being made. If uncertainty begins to affect government decisions and investor perceptions of the country's stability, another concern emerges: how much the government may have to pay when borrowing money.
